zh.title: 美研究指機組員輻射致癌死亡風險居各行業之冠
zh.summary: 美研究顯示機組員輻射致癌死亡風險最高；工會呼籲主管機關實施劑量監測。
body: 據新聞媒體 AeroTime 報導，發表於《美國醫學會雜誌：內科學》（JAMA Internal Medicine）的一項最新研究指出，在美國針對503種職業所進行的分析中，空服員與機師因輻射相關癌症死亡的風險居所有職業之冠，甚至高於直接接觸放射性物質的工人。該研究由哈佛醫學院的維沙爾·帕特爾博士（Dr. Vishal Patel）主持，透過國家衛生統計系統分析2020年至2024年間超過1,200萬份美國死亡證明資料，涵蓋約14,000名機師與7,000名空服員。
研究顯示，在考量各項職業差異後，空服員因輻射相關癌症死亡的機率比一般工作人口高出約50%，機師則高出約36%。在絕對比例方面，輻射相關癌症占空服員總死亡人數的6.9%，占機師總死亡人數的6.7%，而一般工作人口的比例為5%。研究團隊針對白血病、淋巴腫瘤、多發性骨髓瘤以及皮膚癌、乳癌、甲狀腺癌、前列腺癌和中樞神經系統癌症等與輻射相關的癌症進行分析，並排除肺癌以避免吸菸因素干擾結果。
研究人員指出，這兩類機組人員在與輻射無關的癌症死亡率上並未顯著偏高，此一現象顯示其較高的致癌風險更可能源於職場環境中的宇宙輻射暴露，而非生活方式或社會經濟因素。根據美國疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）估計，機組人員每年因飛行航線不同，可能累積3至6毫西弗的宇宙輻射劑量，相較之下，一般旅客每年搭乘約10趟跨國或跨洲來回航班所接收的輻射量僅約0.4毫西弗。
雖然美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）已正式將機師與空服員列為職業性游離輻射暴露群體，但與其他產業的輻射暴露工人或部分國家的機組人員不同，美國目前並未對機組人員實施聯邦輻射劑量上限或強制監測要求。隨附於研究報告的專家評論指出，現代排班模式已大幅減少過往認為導致皮膚癌的高日照停留時間，因此駕駛艙與客艙內的輻射暴露更是主要的風險來源，建議對高空航線機組人員實施定期皮膚檢查與相應篩檢。

研究結果公布後，代表20家航空公司共55,000名空服員的北美空服員協會（AFA-CWA）理事長莎拉·尼爾森（Sara Nelson）發表聲明，呼籲將輻射相關癌症死亡正式認定為因公職災死亡。尼爾森指出，雖然輻射風險已知，但機組人員未獲得相關資訊或培訓，且缺乏明確監管，與歐洲標準不同，FAA至今仍未要求航空公司監測組員的輻射暴露量。工會要求航空業與主管機關採取具體預防措施，並提供職業死亡相關的照護與撫恤保障。

en.title: US Study Finds Aircrew Face Highest Risk of Radiation-Linked Cancer Deaths
en.summary: US study finds pilots and flight attendants face highest radiation cancer mortality; union demands FAA dose monitoring.
body: According to news outlet AeroTime, a new study published in JAMA Internal Medicine has found that US flight attendants and pilots face the highest risk of dying from radiation-related cancers among 503 occupations evaluated, surpassing even workers who directly handle radioactive materials. The research, led by Dr. Vishal Patel of Harvard Medical School, analyzed more than 12 million US death certificates from 2020 to 2024 drawn from the National Vital Statistics System. The dataset covered nearly 13 million decedents across 503 occupations, including approximately 14,000 pilots and 7,000 flight attendants.

The study revealed that flight attendants had roughly 50% higher odds of dying from a radiation-related cancer compared to the general working population, while pilots faced approximately 36% higher odds. In absolute terms, radiation-linked cancers accounted for about 6.9% of flight attendant deaths and 6.7% of pilot deaths, compared with 5% among the general working workforce. Researchers examined deaths from radiation-associated cancers, including leukemia, lymphoma, multiple myeloma, and cancers of the skin, breast, thyroid, prostate, and central nervous system, while explicitly excluding lung cancer to avoid confounding from smoking-related factors.

Neither pilots nor flight attendants exhibited elevated mortality rates from cancers unrelated to radiation. Researchers stated this pattern points to workplace cosmic radiation exposure rather than lifestyle or socioeconomic variables as the primary driver. According to data cited from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, aircrew accumulate an estimated three to six millisieverts of cosmic radiation per year depending on flight paths. This is significantly higher than the approximately 0.4 millisieverts an average air traveler receives annually from about ten cross-country round-trip flights.

While the Federal Aviation Administration formally recognizes pilots and flight attendants as occupationally exposed to ionizing radiation, US aircrew are not subject to federal dose limits or monitoring requirements, unlike radiation-exposed workers in other industries or flight crews in certain other jurisdictions. Commentary accompanying the study noted that modern airline scheduling has largely eliminated the extended layovers once thought to explain high skin cancer rates, pointing instead to cockpit and cabin radiation exposure during high-altitude flights as the principal cause.

Following the publication, Sara Nelson, President of the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, which represents 55,000 flight attendants across 20 airlines, called for radiation-related cancer deaths among aircrew to be formally recognized as occupational deaths. Nelson highlighted that unlike European regulatory frameworks, the FAA does not require airlines to monitor crew exposure to radiation, urging regulators and the aviation industry to establish clear exposure limits, monitoring standards, and medical oversight for flight personnel.

zh.title: F-16V無法如期全數交機 國防部研擬修特別條例延期限
zh.summary: 國防部：66架F-16V因產線排擠無法年底前全數交機，未支用預算將報行政院保留，修訂條例研擬中
body: 國防部依「新式戰機採購特別條例」對美軍購66架F-16V（blk70）戰機，原訂今年底條例到期前全數交機，因產線排擠等因素無法如期完成。國防部8月20日表示，未支用預算將呈報行政院辦理保留，至於是否修訂條例延長期限，現正研擬中，以確保國軍最大權益。
國防部資源司財資處長高志雄少將在下午舉行的記者會中說明，新式戰機採購特別條例在108年由國防部與美軍簽約，屬於已發生債務的契約責任，今年若無法順利支付，將依照預算法、各機關預算作業執行要點呈報行政院辦理保留預算。
空軍透過代號「鳳翔專案」，編列新台幣2472億2883萬元、109年至115年持續性預算，籌購全新66架F-16V（blk70）戰機。由於按特別條例期程，必須在年底前（115年）全數交機，但因產線排擠等因素今年無法如期完成，外界關注是否會修訂條例延長期限。
空軍另以代號「鳳展專案」，由美商洛克希德馬丁與漢翔將140架F-16A/B戰機升級為F-16V（blk20），已在112年12月全數完成。
針對F-16V（blk70）戰機是否近期飛返台灣，國防部副發言人喬福駿少將僅說明，空軍正依規劃全力推動接裝整備工作，管制在計劃節點執行飛返，具體時間仍屬於保密階段，無法說明。
本站紀錄顯示，首批2架F-16V（blk70）戰機已於美東時間8月17日自美國起飛，預計近期飛抵台灣，途中將進行空中加油並停留整備。新購戰機原規劃今年全數返台，因產線搬遷及供應鏈中斷等因素影響有所延宕，美方正採雙班制趕工。

en.title: Taiwan's MND says F-16V deliveries cannot meet year-end deadline, mulls special law amendment
en.summary: MND: 66 F-16V fighters delayed by production line constraints; unused budget to be reserved with Executive Yuan; law amendment under study
body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense (MND) procured 66 F-16V (blk70) fighters from the United States under the New Fighter Procurement Special Act, originally scheduled for full delivery before the act expires at year-end. Due to production line constraints, the deliveries cannot be completed on time. The MND stated on August 20 that unused budget will be reported to the Executive Yuan for reservation, and whether to amend the act to extend the deadline is currently under study to ensure the military's maximum interests.

Maj. Gen. Kao Chih-hsiung, director of the Finance and Information Division of the Resource Planning Office, explained at an afternoon press conference that the New Fighter Procurement Special Act was signed by the MND and the US military in 2019, constituting a contractual obligation of incurred debt. If payment cannot be made this year, the budget will be reported to the Executive Yuan for reservation in accordance with the Budget Act and relevant executive guidelines.

The air force, under the programme codenamed Feng Hsiang, allocated NT$247.22883 billion in sustained budgets from 2020 to 2026 to procure 66 new F-16V (blk70) fighters. Under the special act's timeline, all deliveries must be completed before year-end (2026), but production line constraints and other factors mean the target cannot be met this year, drawing public attention to whether the act will be amended to extend the deadline.

A separate programme, codenamed Feng Jan, upgraded 140 F-16A/B fighters to F-16V (blk20) configuration by Lockheed Martin and Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC), and was fully completed in December 2023.

Regarding whether F-16V (blk70) fighters will fly back to Taiwan in the near term, MND deputy spokesperson Maj. Gen. Chiao Fu-chun stated only that the air force is pushing forward with receiving preparations according to plan, controlling the return flight at planned milestones, with specific timing remaining classified.

AVWIRE records show that the first two F-16V (blk70) fighters departed the United States on August 17 US Eastern Time and are expected to arrive in Taiwan in the near term, with aerial refuelling and stopovers planned en route. The new fighters were originally planned to all return to Taiwan this year but were delayed by production line relocation and supply chain disruptions, with the US side adopting a two-shift schedule to expedite work.
